subject: ventures/persona-conversation-simulator
professional: a negotiation and conflict-skills trainer who runs salary-negotiation role-plays and Thomas-Kilmann (TKI) workshops; first checks: can I enter my own numbers (target, reservation price, the other side's range), is there a zone of possible agreement and do deals stay inside it, does anchoring and concession behaviour follow the bargaining research the page cites, is the Big Five to TKI mapping consistent with the published correlations and honestly labelled, and do the 'who dominates' numbers match what the simulation then does

evidence.correctness: Ran `node /tmp/claude-0/audit-persona/run.mjs`. Passes: the guide's worked example reproduces exactly (Rosa as candidate 57% deal, median 118,000; Linus as candidate 53%, median 102,000; 500 runs, seed 'guide'); over 3,844 simulated deals in the three negotiation scenarios none lands outside both sides' jittered reservation prices (the ZOPA definition); seven hand-computed trait vectors land in the Thomas-Kilmann quadrant their assertiveness/cooperativeness put them in; the runMany median equals a standard median on 169 freelance-rate deals (95). Fails: the group note the page prints next to the cast ('X is likely to dominate the conversation (about 59% of turns)') comes from dynamics.airtime (base 0.35, dynamics.mjs:52), but the simulator speaks with a different rule (base 0.25, 0.15 penalty for the last speaker, and 'ask the quietest', sim.mjs:266); for E95/E5/E50 the note says 59% / 12% / 29%, the 1,000-run simulation gives 46% / 23% / 31%, so the quiet character's airtime is understated by half. The CLI derives persona ids from the first 24 characters of the seed (persona.mjs:67): `node cli.mjs --scenario offsite --seed abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123 --people 3 --runs 200` prints every character at '100% of turns, satisfaction 3.00'. A cast-file trait that is not a number becomes NaN ('ONaN') and runs without an error. Not scored lower because the deal/no-deal and price outputs, which are the headline numbers, are internally consistent and respect the stated limits.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked and working: random seeded cast of 2 to 6, sliders, description-to-traits with negation ('not shy' -> E 83) and intensity, conflict style and 'how to talk to them' tips, pair and group dynamics with named traits, six scenarios (three negotiations, three group decisions), single seeded transcript, 300-run spread with outcome shares, p10/median/p90 price, per-person airtime and satisfaction, copy and JSON download, optional BYOK voicing that throws away any rewrite that changes a number (ai.test.mjs), opt-out local usage counts, CLI with --list/--cast/--runs/--format json and exit code 2 on refusal. Partly: the real-person refusal rejects linkedin, x.com, @handles, emails and phones, but accepts 'github.com/jdoe' and 'youtube.com/@jane' (bare domain links outside its list of social sites). No stubs or TODOs. Served copy clean: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs persona-conversation-simulator` -> no placeholder or retired origin left.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/persona-conversation-simulator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 30 tests, 30 pass, 0.35 s. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: agreeableness concession weight 0.22 -> 0.02 caught; neuroticism walk-away weight removed caught; 'organised' lexicon sign flipped caught; compromising band 9 -> 3 SURVIVED; airtime exponent 1.5 -> 1 SURVIVED; openness-gap friction threshold 40 -> 70 SURVIVED. The tests are invariants (determinism, limits, orderings) plus one pinned worked example; the conflict-style boundaries, the airtime percentages the page prints and most pair rules are not pinned, and no test compares the dynamics airtime note with the simulator's own airtime.
evidence.craft: Read persona.mjs (231 lines), dynamics.mjs (74), sim.mjs (404), ai.mjs (77), cli.mjs (76), index.html script, all three test files. @ts-check throughout, pure seeded functions, no dependencies, the page builds DOM with textContent (no injection), BYOK client is a byte-checked synced copy. Defects: persona id truncated to 24 seed characters so long seeds give every character the same id (persona.mjs:67), corrupting turn counts and satisfaction keyed by id; cast-file traits are not validated (NaN flows through clamp); two independent airtime formulas for the same quantity (dynamics.mjs:52 vs sim.mjs:266); negation only looks one or two words back ('not at all shy' reads as shy, E 28).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'not fitted to data', 'rehearsal aid, not a forecast', fictional-only notice and its reasons, no-warranty and no-SLA disclaimers on both pages and README, BYOK note that a rewrite changing a number is discarded (ai.test.mjs), 'page itself makes no network calls' (page.test.mjs), the guide's 57% / 118,000 and 53% / 102,000 table (rerun above). Not backed: guide line 62 says Barry and Friedman (1998) found agreeableness and extraversion liabilities in distributive bargaining and 'the simulator's concession sizes follow that direction'; concession size (sim.mjs:162) does not use extraversion, and extraversion raises the opening anchor (sim.mjs:116), so a more extraverted candidate does slightly better (median 110,000 at E10, 111,000 at E50, 112,000 at E90, 1,000 runs each), the opposite of the cited finding; agreeableness does follow it (116,000 / 111,000 / 105,000 at A10/50/90). The page's 'about 59% of turns' note is not what the simulator does (correctness). 'Refuses profile links' (index.html:135, README.md:20) is partial: github.com and youtube.com links pass. The footer's list of counted events (index.html:149) omits ai_voice_run, which the page records (index.html:255).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through as a trainer preparing a salary-negotiation exercise: I can build two characters, read their styles, and show a class how often a blunt candidate against an agreeable manager closes and where. But every scenario's numbers are fixed in sim.mjs (salary target 125,000 / floor 102,000 against 98,000 / 118,000; freelance 130/85 against 75/110; used car 14,500/11,800 against 10,500/13,200) and cannot be changed on the page or CLI, so a person rehearsing their own salary cannot enter their range or their counterpart's budget, there is never a no-ZOPA case, and nobody can play a seat (the VENTURE.yaml lists that as a later tier). The lines are templates, so transcripts repeat quickly unless the user brings an AI key. For writers and for teaching the idea of conflict styles it works; for the README's first use, 'rehearse a hard conversation', it does not yet.
evidence.domain: Negotiation mechanics match standard distributive-bargaining practice: each side has a target and a reservation price, deals stay inside the ZOPA, concessions are a share of the remaining gap so they shrink as the parties converge, and impasse is possible despite a ZOPA. Departures: the Big Five to TKI mapping is a hand-made heuristic (disclosed) and parts of it run against the published correlations I know of (Antonioni 1998, Int. J. Conflict Management, cited from memory, not fetched): avoiding there correlates with higher agreeableness and neuroticism and lower extraversion, while the tool's avoiding needs low agreeableness and ignores neuroticism; conscientiousness, linked to integrating, is unused. Over 10,000 random characters the styles split avoiding 9%, collaborating 9%, compromising 27%, accommodating 28%, competing 27%. The extraversion effect on outcomes runs opposite to the Barry and Friedman finding the guide cites. Description lexicon checked against Saucier's (1994) 40 Mini-Markers: 23 read in the right direction, 1 mis-keyed ('practical', a Conscientiousness marker, is read as low Openness, persona.mjs:174), 16 unrecognised (e.g. extraverted, sympathetic, systematic, temperamental, intellectual).

defects.what: The group note's airtime figure ('likely to dominate the conversation (about 59% of turns)', 'speak least') comes from dynamics.airtime with base weight 0.35, while the simulator picks speakers with base 0.25, a last-speaker penalty and 'ask the quietest'. For E95/E5/E50 the note says 59/12/29% and the simulation gives 46/23/31%, so the page contradicts its own 300-run table and halves the quiet character's share.

The guide says the simulator follows Barry and Friedman (1998) for both agreeableness and extraversion; extraversion is not in the concession size and raises the opening anchor, so more extraverted candidates do slightly better (110k / 111k / 112k at E10/50/90), the opposite of the cited finding.

Scenario numbers (targets and reservation prices) are hard-coded and not editable on the page or CLI, so a user cannot rehearse their own salary, rate or price, and every scenario always has a ZOPA. The README's first listed use is rehearsing a hard conversation.

Persona ids are the first 24 characters of the seed, so a CLI seed of about 22+ characters gives every character the same id; speaker selection, airtime and satisfaction (keyed by id) collapse: each character reports '100% of turns, satisfaction 3.00'.

Big Five to TKI mapping departs from the published correlations (Antonioni 1998: avoiding rises with agreeableness and neuroticism; conscientiousness relates to integrating): the tool's avoiding requires low agreeableness and neither neuroticism nor conscientiousness enters. Disclosed as a heuristic.

Lexicon keys 'practical' as low Openness; in Saucier's (1994) Mini-Markers it is a Conscientiousness (+) marker. 16 of the 40 Mini-Markers (extraverted, sympathetic, systematic, temperamental, intellectual ...) are not recognised.
checkFictional accepts bare-domain profile links outside its social-site list ('github.com/jdoe', 'youtube.com/@jane'), while the page and README say it refuses profile links.
Cast-file traits are not validated: a non-numeric trait becomes NaN, prints 'ONaN' and the run exits 0.

Three of six seeded mutants survive: the compromising band, the airtime exponent and the openness-gap threshold are not pinned by any test, and nothing checks the dynamics airtime note against the simulator.
Footer lists the counted events as sim_run, many_run, character_added, export_used but the page also records ai_voice_run (README lists it).

verdict: A careful, honest prototype that does what it says but not yet at a negotiation trainer's bar. The negotiation engine is sound where it can be checked: the guide's 57% / $118,000 and 53% / $102,000 example reproduces exactly, 3,844 simulated deals all fall inside both sides' reservation prices, and the conflict-style quadrants follow the Thomas-Kilmann definitions. Disclaimers, the fictional-only refusal and 'not fitted to data' are prominent and true. It misses the bar on three counts. First, the page's 'about 59% of turns' dominance note uses a different formula from the simulator, which gives 46%, and halves the quiet character's share. Second, the guide says the engine follows Barry and Friedman for extraversion, but extraversion helps in the simulation. Third, half the seeded mutants survive. For the job it advertises first, rehearsing your own salary conversation, the scenario numbers are fixed in code, so a user cannot enter their own range. Smaller defects: long CLI seeds collapse every character to one id, 'practical' is mis-keyed against Saucier's markers, and bare-domain profile links pass the refusal.
